On behalf of our board of directors, our staff, and the survivors we serve every day, I want to extend our gratitude to Mayor Woodfin and the Birmingham City Council for your efforts and support in bringing awareness to and recognizing the importance of addressing domestic violence in our community. Domestic violence is a public health and a public safety crisis in Birmingham.

It is not just something that takes place in the home behind closed doors. In fact, just last week, Chief Pickett shared that while total violent crime is down, domestic violence cases are up 18%. This spills out into our neighborhoods through violence, addiction, homelessness, joblessness, physical and mental health issues, and through our children.

Domestic violence perpetuates the generational cycle of violence, poverty, and trauma that affects so many communities. So as we work to lead a coordinated community response to domestic and sexual violence that protects survivors, promotes healing, and holds offenders accountable, I stand here representing not just the team at one place,

But of all the community partners that join us in this work, Birmingham Police Department, the YWCA, the Hispanic and Immigrant Center of Alabama, Legal Services of Alabama, the Crisis Center, Safe House of Shelby County, the Black Women's Mental Health Institute, UAB Medical Center,

The Jefferson County Sheriff's Office, the District Attorney's Office, the U.S. Attorney's Office, Birmingham Municipal Courts, our City Attorney's Office, and the City of Birmingham, just to name a few. It is not on an individual victim to solve their domestic violence crisis. It is the responsibility of all of us. We are all in this together. We must be part of the solution.

Thank you for joining us in this work to build safer communities where survivors are believed and our systems work together, united against domestic and sexual violence. Systems that ensure safety and justice for survivors help to break the cycle of generational violence and uphold the belief that everyone has the right to live a life that is safe and free of violence.
